data.narrative:
Echodyne, a Series C defense and security technology company that has raised $224M to date, sits within a competitive peer universe of 12 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies comprising 2 public and 10 private firms. Key comparables include Quantum-Systems ($8.0B, Series C), Helsing ($18.0B, Series D), and Saronic ($9.2B, Series D), with the peer set ranging from $300M to $18.0B in valuation.

Two valuation methods prove applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C advancement, yielding $381M based on the $224M capital raised proxy. Peer-median benchmarking across the 12-company cohort produces $1.8B, reflecting the wide dispersion inherent in frontier-defense valuations where capabilities and strategic positioning drive substantial variance.

Triangulation of these two methods produces a valuation range of $324M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $1.1B. The wide spread reflects material uncertainty around stage timing, product maturity, and customer traction relative to the peer set—which spans from early-stage defense plays valued near $300M to later-stage platforms commanding $18B+. Resolution of this range depends on near-term evidence of customer adoption, technology differentiation, and path to next funding round.
